textinformation.text: MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT
Dedicated Delivery Center Engagement
This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) takes effect on March 17, 2025 (the “Effective Date”) and is made between:
(1) HALCYON RETAIL GROUP, LLC, a Texas limited liability company with its principal office at 4200 Commerce Street, Suite 1100, Dallas, Texas 75226, USA (“Client”); and

(2) MERIDIAN BYTECRAFT INC., a Delaware corporation with its principal office at 77 Harbor Point Drive, Suite 300, Wilmington, Delaware 19801, USA, and MERIDIAN BYTECRAFT SOLUTIONS PRIVATE LIMITED, a company incorporated in India with its registered office in Pune, Maharashtra (together, “Provider”).
Client and Provider are each a “Party” and together the “Parties”.
BACKGROUND

(A) Provider operates offshore technology delivery centers and wishes to supply to Client, and Client wishes to purchase from Provider, the services described in this Agreement on the terms set out below.
(B) The Parties have held detailed discussions on the shape of the relationship and have recorded their conclusions in this Agreement.
In consideration of the mutual promises below, the Parties agree as follows:
ARTICLE 1	INTERPRETATION AND DEFINED TERMS
1.1	Defined Terms. Capitalised expressions used in this Agreement carry the meanings assigned to them in Schedule A (Glossary), unless the context plainly requires another meaning.
1.2	Rules of Construction.
(a) Every Schedule forms an integral part of this Agreement, and a mention of “this Agreement” covers the Schedules and any appendices annexed to them.
(b) Captions, the contents page and the schedule list are provided only for ease of navigation and have no bearing on how the Agreement is read or enforced.
(c) A cross-reference to an Article, Section or Schedule points to that item of this Agreement unless the text says otherwise.
(d) A mention of any statute or regulation includes that statute or regulation as amended, re-enacted or replaced from time to time.
(e) Whenever the words “including”, “includes” or “such as” appear, they are to be read as introducing examples and not as a limit (“without limitation” is implied).
(f) The singular covers the plural and the reverse, where that fits the context.

(g) Both Parties took part in shaping the wording of this Agreement with the help of counsel. No ambiguity will be resolved against a Party merely because that Party, or its lawyers, prepared the first draft; the text will be read to give effect to the Parties’ shared intention as shown by the Agreement taken as a whole.

1.3	Hierarchy of Documents. If the main body of this Agreement and a Schedule or Work Order say different things, the main body governs, save where the Schedule or Work Order expressly states that it is intended to override a named provision of the main body.
ARTICLE 2	DURATION

2.1	Initial Period. This Agreement starts on the Effective Date and remains in force for thirty-six (36) months (the “Initial Period”), subject to any earlier termination permitted by this Agreement or any later date reached through a Renewal Period.

2.2	Automatic Renewal. When the Initial Period ends, and when each Renewal Period ends, this Agreement renews for a further twelve (12) months (each a “Renewal Period”), unless either Party gives the other written notice of non-renewal at least one hundred twenty (120) days before the current period expires. Provider may update the rates for a Renewal Period by giving Client written notice of the revised rates not less than one hundred fifty (150) days before the renewal date, and Client’s failure to give notice of non-renewal means the revised rates apply.
ARTICLE 3	THE SERVICES

3.1	Scope of Core Services. “Core Services” are the functions and tasks Provider has agreed in writing to carry out for Client in each Service Stream, as set out in this Agreement, the Onboarding Plan and the Work Orders, and as they may be modified by an approved Change Request. Core Services comprise only:
(a) the activities described for each Service Stream in the Onboarding Plan and every Work Order;

(b) tasks that were previously handled by the Client Employees and Client Contractors who moved to Provider under this Agreement, but only where those tasks are listed in a Work Order or have been added through the Change Control Procedure;
(c) the supply and periodic renewal of the Provider Technology Stack used by the Delivery Team; and
(d) a joint effort, to be agreed in writing, to evaluate extending Provider’s CMMI-based quality certification to Client’s software lines, at the pace and cost the Parties settle in a Work Order.
Work not covered by this Section 3.1 is outside the Core Services and is chargeable at the Rate Card once authorised through a Change Request.
3.2	How Services Are Delivered.

(a) Start Dates and Onboarding. From the Effective Date Provider will carry out the Onboarding Services described in the Onboarding Plan. The plan lists several Service Start Dates and the Services attached to each. From each Service Start Date, Provider will perform the Services allocated to it. Client may state its scheduling preferences through the process in the Operations Handbook, and Provider will take them into account in a commercially reasonable way, consistent with Provider’s staffing and its other commitments.
(b) Core Services. Provider will perform the Core Services as stated in this Agreement, the Onboarding Plan and each Work Order.

(c) Additional Headcount. If Client asks for extra work in a Service Stream that cannot be handled with the Delivery Team in place when the request is made, Provider will, within fifteen (15) business days, tell Client whether it can supply further staff and, if so, estimate the number needed and the timeline (the “Added Headcount”). Provider is not required to accept an expansion. Added Headcount will be provided only once the Governance Board signs a written addendum, at the rates stated in Schedule B, and Client is liable only for Added Headcount that it has approved in writing. An expansion approved under this Section is an enlargement of an existing Service Stream and is not a New Service Stream.

(d) Headcount Reduction. After the first twelve (12) months from the Effective Date, and on at least ninety (90) days’ written notice, Client may lower the size of the Delivery Team once per calendar quarter, by no more than ten percent (10%) of the preceding quarter’s average team size, or three (3) people, whichever is larger. Charges drop from the effective date of the reduction, but Client must pay the Reduction Charge in Schedule B to compensate Provider for bench time, severance and redeployment costs, and the Minimum Commitment continues to apply.

(e) Taking Work Elsewhere. Client may move part of the Services in-house or to another vendor only on at least ninety (90) days’ written notice, and the Minimum Commitment, together with the Reduction Charge, will continue to apply to the work removed.

(f) Client Group Members. Provider will perform the Services for Client and those Client Affiliates that Client has identified in writing and that have signed a joinder. Client is responsible for each Client Affiliate’s compliance and payment. Where this Agreement imposes duties or licences on Provider, “Client” includes only those Affiliates that have joined.

(g) Infrastructure. Unless this Agreement states otherwise, Provider will furnish the premises, equipment, connectivity and software that it chooses to use to deliver the Services. Shared common services are described in Schedule M. The location and standards of the Delivery Center are described in Schedule F. Upon at least five (5) business days’ written notice, Provider will let Client’s authorised staff visit the areas of the Provider Sites where the Services are performed during business hours, accompanied by a Provider escort, and subject to Provider’s security rules and the confidentiality rights of Provider’s other customers.

(h) Delivery and Acceptance. Provider will hand over each Deliverable in accordance with the relevant Work Order. If the Work Order sets Acceptance Tests, the Deliverable must meet them in all material respects; otherwise it will be tested against the written specifications that the Parties approved for that Deliverable. Provider will carry out internal testing before delivery and will tell Client of any known non-conformity. Client has ten (10) business days from delivery to test the Deliverable and to either accept it or give a written list of reproducible non-conformities. If Client does neither within that window, the Deliverable is deemed accepted, and it is also deemed accepted when Client puts it into production use. Provider will correct reported non-conformities within a reasonable period, and Client then has five (5) business days to retest. Repair or re-performance of a non-conforming Deliverable, or, if repair is not feasible, a refund of the fees paid for that Deliverable, is Client’s sole remedy for non-conformity.

3.3	Technology Improvements. Provider will review its technology and delivery methods at least once in every twelve (12) months and, at one of the Governance Board’s regular meetings, will brief Client on developments that Provider reasonably thinks could benefit the Services. Any proposal to adopt a new technology or method will be handled as a Change Request, under which Client decides whether to adopt it and agrees to any resulting change in fees. Provider is not required to adopt any technology beyond the level that is generally used in the offshore software-services industry for similar work.

3.4	Permits and Regulatory Approvals. Each Party will obtain, at its own expense, the permits, licences and registrations that the law applying to it requires in order to perform its own obligations. Where one Party asks, the other will give reasonable assistance, with any out-of-pocket costs borne by the requesting Party.
3.5	Legal and Regulatory Change.

(a) Monitoring. Client will watch for, and give Provider prompt notice of, any change in law in the places where Client operates that affects the Services or Client’s use of them (“Client Law Changes”). Provider will watch for, and give Client prompt notice of, changes in the law of the country in which the Delivery Center is located that directly affect Provider’s performance (“Provider Law Changes”).
(b) Consequences.

(i) Client Law Changes. The Parties will consult on the revisions to the Services needed for compliance. Provider will quote any fee impact within a reasonable time, and will carry out the revisions once Client approves the quote through the Change Control Procedure.

(ii) Provider Law Changes. Provider will implement such changes to the way it delivers the Services as are required for compliance with a Provider Law Change at its own cost, except that costs attributable to immigration, visa and wage rules, and any cost that has a significant effect on Provider’s cost of delivery, will be borne by Client as an equitable fee adjustment to which the Parties will agree in good faith.

(iii) Material Impact. If a change in law, or a change in the Services needed to comply with it, outside either Party’s reasonable control, lowers the Delivery Team below the level permitted by Section 3.2(d), Provider may, at its choice, (A) propose a fair adjustment to the fees, which the Parties will negotiate, or (B) end the affected part of the Services on notice. Client will pay all charges for work performed and unrecoverable costs incurred up to the end date.

3.6	Client Technology Standards. Provider will use the minimum hardware and software configuration and communication lines listed in Schedule H, and will observe the technical standards of Client that have been given to Provider in writing. If Client later modifies those standards, Provider will adopt the modified standards through the Change Control Procedure, with any added cost charged to Client.

3.7	Knowledge Transfer. In the sixty (60) days leading up to expiry or termination, and on Client’s reasonable request, Provider will make appropriate staff available to describe (a) how the Deliverables work and are operated, (b) the testing approach and scripts, (c) the development workflow, (d) how the Services are provided, and (e) such documentation as Client reasonably needs to run the delivered Systems after the Agreement ends. Up to forty (40) hours of this support is included in the fees; further hours are billable at the Rate Card.

3.8	Reporting. Provider will submit the reports listed in Schedule I in the format stated there and any other reports agreed in a Work Order. Reports Client requests in addition to those will be prepared at the Rate Card, unless they take less than two (2) hours.

3.9	Project Planning and Progress Tracking. The Parties will together prepare and maintain delivery plans for the Services, which Provider will supply on request in a mutually agreed form. Provider will measure progress against milestones using accepted industry practice and will report status each week for the first two (2) quarters and every month thereafter, or as the Operations Handbook states. A delay in a milestone caused by Client or by a Client Third-Party Vendor extends the milestone by a matching period.

3.10	Equipment Acquisition. Where Client asks Provider to acquire Additional Equipment, Provider will, if it agrees to do so, seek competitive terms from vendors and Client may choose either (i) to lend the equipment to Provider for use solely for Client’s work, or (ii) to have Provider obtain it by purchase, lease or licence (alone or through a third party) on terms that Provider has disclosed and Client has approved in writing. Provider will pass through to Client any volume discounts it actually receives on the specific purchase, after deducting a handling fee of five percent (5%). Client will reimburse the actual purchase, lease or licence price and transport costs. Unless otherwise agreed, (1) title to equipment bought by Provider for Client passes to Client once Client has paid in full, (2) the equipment will be new, and (3) the party that arranges shipment bears the risk of loss during transit, while Client bears the risk of loss or damage to Client-owned equipment kept at a Provider Site, except to the extent caused by Provider’s negligence. Supplier warranties on the equipment are passed through to Client to the extent they are assignable. At Client’s request and expense, Provider will return Client-owned equipment to Client.
ARTICLE 4	ONBOARDING; ACQUISITIONS AND DIVESTITURES; COLLABORATION

4.1	Onboarding Services. Provider will carry out the activities needed to move the Services into Provider’s Delivery Center (the “Onboarding Services”), which are expected to take about six (6) months, in line with the Onboarding Plan and without causing unreasonable disruption to Client’s operations. Schedule J is the starting framework for the final Onboarding Plan, which the Parties will complete together no later than forty-five (45) days after the Effective Date. Provider will name an Onboarding Lead, and a point person for each Client site or function affected, who will brief Client’s Account Lead on progress at reasonable intervals.

4.2	Onboarding Milestones. Provider will use reasonable efforts to hit the Onboarding Milestones set out in the Onboarding Plan. If Provider misses a Critical Onboarding Milestone for reasons not attributable to Client, a Client Third-Party Vendor, or a Force Majeure Event, and then does not complete the milestone within the Cure Window, Client may end the affected Service Stream on written notice, in which case no Early Exit Charge is payable but Client will pay for work performed and costs incurred up to that point. Client will give Provider timely warning of any perceived slippage, including at Governance Board meetings.

4.3	Employees Moving to Provider. Provider will make employment offers, on Provider’s standard terms and in accordance with Provider’s ordinary hiring criteria, to those Client personnel whom the Parties agree should move to Provider (“Moved Personnel”), and will use reasonable efforts to have at least seventy percent (70%) of them accept. Provider’s offer to or employment of any individual does not oblige it to retain that individual beyond what its own business needs require.
4.4	Corporate Changes on Client’s Side.

(a) New Group Members. If Client acquires another business, is itself acquired, or adds further Affiliates (“New Group Members”), then, provided that serving them would not breach Provider’s existing exclusivity commitments to another customer, Provider will, on Client’s request and at the Rate Card, assist in integrating the New Group Members’ IT environments into the Systems and, if the Parties agree through a Change Request, supply Services to them.

(b) Carve-Outs. If Client sells a business unit or ceases to include an Affiliate (“Carve-Out Entities”), Provider will, on request, keep serving the Carve-Out Entity for up to six (6) months on the then-applicable terms, provided that the entity signs a joinder accepting this Agreement and satisfies Provider’s credit review. Provider will also, at the Rate Card, support Client, the Carve-Out Entity and the purchaser in separating the relevant IT environments.
(c) Added Costs. Client will bear all additional costs triggered by events described in this Section 4.4, with Provider giving prior notice of the nature and expected amount of such costs.

4.5	Working With Client’s Other Vendors. Client may from time to time engage other contractors or consultants (“Client Third-Party Vendors”). Provider will cooperate in good faith with them as reasonably requested, on condition that Client ensures each Client Third-Party Vendor signs confidentiality terms acceptable to Provider. Cooperation may include:
(a) giving written requirements, standards and policies for the Services, to the extent they exist, so the vendor’s work can be integrated;
(b) giving written interface requirements for the vendor’s work;
(c) giving written requirements for any needed changes to the Systems;
(d) making its own testing processes available to the extent they relate to the vendor’s work;
(e) providing reasonable assistance so the vendor or Client can learn how to run and maintain the vendor’s work as part of the Systems, with Provider’s effort billed at the Rate Card; and

(f) providing access to Provider’s software, equipment and sites needed for the vendor’s work, as long as Provider approves in advance, may impose security conditions and may withhold access that would compromise other customers.
Client is answerable for the acts and omissions of every Client Third-Party Vendor. Provider is not obliged to disclose its proprietary methods or tools.
ARTICLE 5	ADDITIONAL SERVICE STREAMS

5.1	Requests for New Streams. During the Term and any Exit Support Period, Client may ask Provider to supply services beyond the current scope (a “New Service Stream”). Provider will respond to the request, within twenty (20) business days (or any other period the Parties agree), either by declining or by giving a written proposal (a “New Stream Proposal”), which will cover:
(a) a description of the work Provider expects to perform;
(b) a timetable for the start and, where relevant, the end of the work;
(c) Provider’s estimate of the people needed, with a breakdown;
(d) when relevant, any new software or equipment that would be required;
(e) when relevant, the runtime and development environment requirements;
(f) the skills profile of the staff proposed;
(g) when relevant, existing software or equipment that would be used;
(h) when relevant, acceptance criteria and test procedures; and
(i) any other details Client reasonably asks for.

Provider will not start work on a New Service Stream before both Parties have agreed the terms and Client’s Account Lead has countersigned the New Stream Proposal. Any work that Provider performs before then at Client’s request is billable at the Rate Card.

5.2	Pricing of New Streams. Charges for a New Service Stream will be set in the New Stream Proposal on the basis of the Rate Card and the resources and skills required, and will be consistent with Provider’s then-current market pricing for comparable work. Where work for a New Service Stream replaces resources already billed under existing Services, the Parties will discuss in good faith a fair offset.

5.3	Work Placed With Other Vendors. If Client chooses to have a vendor that is not a direct competitor of Provider carry out any New Service Stream work, Provider will cooperate reasonably with Client and that vendor in accordance with Section 4.5.
ARTICLE 6	CLIENT OBLIGATIONS

6.1	Client Account Lead. Client will designate a person (the “Client Account Lead”) to act as Client’s main representative from the Effective Date. The Client Account Lead will (a) oversee and coordinate Client’s compliance with its duties, and (b) have power to bind Client on all matters relating to this Agreement, including by giving decisions, approvals and instructions within three (3) business days of request. The Client Account Lead may pass on tasks to other Client staff after informing Provider.
6.2	What Client Provides.

(a) Premises. From each Service Start Date, and for as long as Provider needs them to carry out the relevant Services, Client will make available at no charge to Provider the space at the Client Sites listed in Schedule F, along with reasonable furniture, cleaning, desk telephones, parking, access to computers, servers and printers and utilities, to at least the standard Client gives its own contractors. Client will also supply the productivity equipment that Provider’s on-site staff reasonably need. Client Sites are made available in their present condition.

(b) Systems Access. Client will give Provider timely access to those Client systems, information, documentation, licences and personnel that Provider needs to deliver the Services. Provider will use the access only for the Services and will follow the written security and conduct policies Client has supplied to it. Client is responsible for the accuracy and completeness of the information and materials it provides.

6.3	Provider Use of Client Sites. Provider and its personnel may use the Client Sites for providing the Services, and nothing in this Agreement grants Provider a tenancy. In connection with those sites:
(a) Provider will follow the requirements in this Article 6 and Schedule F;
(b) Provider will make reasonable and efficient use of the space;

(c) Provider will keep the space tidy, avoid damage, not use it for any unlawful aim, and follow Client’s reasonable site rules that were notified to Provider, and will be responsible for damage and fines it causes through its negligence;
(d) Provider will allow Client to enter the areas occupied by Provider’s staff, on reasonable notice, for maintenance work;
(e) Provider will not make structural, mechanical or electrical alterations without Client’s written consent, and any alteration will belong to Client or its landlords; and
(f) when a Client Site is no longer needed, Provider will return it in substantially the condition received, apart from fair wear and tear.

6.4	Effect of Client Non-Performance. If Client fails to carry out any of its obligations under this Agreement, including through delay in providing decisions, access, data, premises, third-party cooperation or approvals (a “Client Delay”), then, to the extent the Client Delay affects Provider’s performance: (a) Provider is relieved of the affected obligations and of the related Service Levels and Service Credits; (b) delivery dates are extended by a matching period; and (c) Provider may charge for the additional costs reasonably caused by the Client Delay, at the Rate Card. Provider will tell Client about a Client Delay within ten (10) business days after becoming aware of it and will make reasonable efforts to limit its impact. Client’s failure to pay fees is additionally governed by Article 24.
ARTICLE 7	PERFORMANCE STANDARDS

7.1	Service Levels. Provider will provide the Services in line with the Service Levels set out in Schedule C and the relevant Work Order. A Work Order may state that particular Service Levels, or Schedule C as a whole, do not apply to that Work Order. For Services with no stated Service Levels, Provider will perform with the care and skill that is customary in the industry.

7.2	Service Level Review. In the final quarter of every Contract Year, on Client’s request, the Governance Board will examine the Service Levels for the year just ending and, by agreement, adjust any that have become unsuitable because the Services have changed or for another good reason, with the revised levels applying for the following Contract Year. Client may also, at any time on notice, ask for an out-of-cycle review, but no Service Level changes unless both Parties sign a written amendment.

7.3	Failure Analysis. After a failure to meet a Service Level that is within Provider’s control, Provider will, within ten (10) business days, (a) carry out a root-cause review, (b) deliver to Client a summary of the cause and the remedy proposed, and (c) once Client approves the remedy, put it in place using commercially reasonable efforts. If the work cannot be completed within the ten-day period, Provider will give Client regular progress reports until it is done. Provider is not required to analyse failures caused by Client Delay, Force Majeure Events, or events excluded under Schedule C.

7.4	Measurement Tools. From each Service Start Date Provider will use the measurement and monitoring tools and processes agreed in Schedule C for the relevant Services. The tools will produce reports detailed enough to show whether Service Levels have been met, and Client may, once a year, on reasonable notice and at its own cost, inspect them through its auditor. Provider will make the Systems used to supply the Services compatible with the Client software and equipment identified in the Onboarding Plan that is meant to exchange records with them.

7.5	Ongoing Improvement. Alongside any improvement obligations in Schedule C, Provider will from time to time put forward, for Client’s consideration, techniques and tools used elsewhere in its operations that Provider believes could improve the Services, and will mention them in the periodic reports described in Section 3.8. Adopting any such proposal is subject to the Change Control Procedure.

7.6	Service Credits. If Provider fails to meet a Service Level, Client’s remedy is the Service Credit specified in Schedule C, which Provider will apply on the next invoice. Provider will not owe a Service Credit if the failure was caused by Client Delay, Client’s refusal to approve sufficient Delivery Team capacity, a Force Majeure Event, scheduled maintenance, or Client Third-Party Vendors. If Provider tells Client within ten (10) days of a failure that it was caused by such a factor, the Parties will take the matter to Section 23.1 and the Service Credit is suspended until resolved. In no month will the Service Credits exceed ten percent (10%) of the monthly fees for the affected Service Stream. Service Credits are Client’s sole and exclusive financial remedy for a failure to meet a Service Level, without prejudice to Client’s termination right under Section 24.3(b)(i).
ARTICLE 8	CLIENT FEEDBACK SURVEYS

8.1	Satisfaction Surveys. Within one hundred eighty (180) days of the Effective Date the Parties will choose an independent survey firm and agree the method for conducting satisfaction surveys of Client’s internal stakeholders on the Services, as described in Schedule K. The first baseline survey will be completed within a further ninety (90) days, with its questions approved by both Parties before it goes out. Later surveys will take place annually. The Parties may agree to treat results as a reference point for improvements in Schedule C, but survey scores do not by themselves constitute a Service Level or a breach. Each Party will bear half of the survey firm’s charges.

8.2	Contested Results. If Client disagrees with a survey’s results, it may, at its own expense and after consulting Provider, commission one further survey by a different independent firm. The Parties will review both sets of results together in good faith, but neither survey is binding.
ARTICLE 9	PRICE BENCHMARKING

9.1	Selecting a Benchmarker. After the third (3rd) anniversary of the Effective Date, and not more than once in any twenty-four (24) months, Client may request a benchmarking exercise. The exercise will be performed by an independent firm jointly selected from the list in Schedule L, and Client will pay the firm’s charges. If no listed firm is available, the Parties will agree a substitute within thirty (30) business days, failing which each side will nominate a firm and those two firms will pick the benchmarker. Provider will cooperate reasonably, including by giving data about its fees, at Client’s cost for time over twenty (20) hours.

9.2	Scope and Method. The benchmarker will compare the fees and service levels for the selected Services against those for comparable services, taking into account volume, scope, tenure, geography, technology, term and risk profile, and will give both Parties the opportunity to comment on its methodology and draft findings before issuing them.

9.3	Results and Follow-Up. The Parties will study the findings during a sixty (60) day review period. If the benchmarker concludes, on a like-for-like basis, that Provider’s fees for a Service exceed the comparable market range by more than fifteen percent (15%), the Parties will negotiate in good faith an adjustment to the fees or the Service Levels, but no adjustment is made without both Parties’ agreement and no retroactive reduction applies.
ARTICLE 10	DELIVERY LOCATIONS AND SECURITY

10.1	Approved Locations. The Services will be delivered from (a) the Provider Sites, (b) the Client Sites, and (c) any other place agreed in writing, in each case as noted in Schedules B and F. Provider may deliver Services for several customers from a Provider Site. Neither Provider nor its personnel will market or deliver third-party services from a Client Site without Client’s consent.

10.2	Changing Locations. Provider may add or replace a Provider Site in the same country (or, if the Parties have agreed to additional countries, within those countries) on thirty (30) days’ notice to Client, provided there is no material adverse impact on the Services. To move delivery outside those countries, Provider will give Client a written proposal describing the new location, the reasons, the expected effect on the Services and any anticipated fee changes, and Client will not unreasonably withhold approval. Client will bear the additional costs it incurs because Provider relocates at Client’s request, while Provider will bear the additional costs it causes by relocating for its own reasons.

10.3	Physical Safety and Security. Provider will operate, at each Provider Site, safety and security procedures that are commercially reasonable and not less protective than those described in Schedule F, and will comply with Client’s written site rules while at Client Sites. If Client asks for measures stronger than those in Schedule F, Client will bear the extra cost.

10.4	Information Security. Provider will maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards intended to protect Client Data in its custody against destruction, loss, unauthorised alteration and unauthorised access, in accordance with the security program in Schedule E (“Security Measures”), which will be no less protective than the standards of the industry for similar services and the law that applies to Provider. Either Party may propose updates to the Security Measures, which take effect once agreed through the Change Control Procedure. If Provider learns of an actual breach of security affecting Client Data, it will (a) inform Client’s Account Lead without undue delay and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours, and (b) investigate, take reasonable steps to contain and remedy the breach, and give Client a summary of the corrective measures. Client may keep its own backup copies of Client Data.

10.5	Separation of Client Data. Provider will implement policies, consistent with Schedule E, that logically separate Client Data from the data of its other customers and restrict access to Client’s Confidential Information to those staff who need it to perform the Services.
ARTICLE 11	PROVIDER PERSONNEL

11.1	Recruiting and Assignment. Provider alone decides how to recruit, hire, train, supervise and compensate its personnel, subject to the standards in Schedule N. Before putting a person into a Key Staff role, Provider will tell Client about the proposed assignment and share a profile of the individual, and Client may interview that person and raise reasonable objections within three (3) business days, which Provider will consider in good faith. Provider will try to keep Key Staff assigned for the periods stated in Schedule N and will, together with Client, consider sensible steps to reduce staff turnover, at Client’s cost where those steps go beyond Provider’s normal practices.

11.2	Provider Account Lead. Provider will name a person (the “Provider Account Lead”) as its principal representative from the Effective Date, who will (a) oversee Provider’s performance of the Agreement and (b) be authorised to act for Provider in matters relating to the Agreement. The Provider Account Lead may be assigned to other duties in addition to this account.
11.3	Key Staff.
(a) The Parties will jointly identify the roles that count as Key Staff in Schedule N.
(b) Provider will keep a succession approach for Key Staff who leave the account for any reason and, on request, will describe that approach to Client.
(c) Provider will make Key Staff reasonably available to meet Client’s personnel in line with the Operations Handbook.
11.4	Delivery Team.

(a) Selection. Provider will place on the Delivery Team individuals with the training and skills suited to their roles, consistent with the skill mix in the Work Orders. Team members will be allocated to Client’s account for the percentage of working time specified in the Work Order. Every ninety (90) days Provider will give Client a roster showing job titles. On Client’s written request, and at Client’s cost, Provider will carry out and confirm background verification that is permitted by local law and in line with Provider’s policy, for Delivery Team members who will work at a Client Site for more than five (5) days.

(b) Direction of the Team. Client may direct the day-to-day priorities of the Delivery Team through Provider’s managers, but Provider remains responsible for the personnel’s employment and for the manner of their work. Delivery Team members on Client’s premises will work only on Client-related matters unless Provider and Client agree otherwise. Provider will make sure each Delivery Team member is bound by written confidentiality and invention-assignment commitments that are enforceable under local law.
(c) Replacement. Provider will notify Client of the departure or reassignment of any Delivery Team member in a timely way. Nothing here requires Provider to end anyone’s employment.

(i) If Client reasonably objects to the conduct of a person at a Client Site, Provider will promptly investigate and, where warranted, remove that person from the Client Site and replace them within a reasonable period.

(ii) If Client has documented cause (such as serious misconduct or a security violation) to demand the removal of a Delivery Team member, Provider will remove that individual from the account within forty-eight (48) hours and propose a replacement as soon as practical.

(iii) If Client reasonably contends that a team member is not performing adequately, it will tell Provider in writing, and Provider may propose a corrective plan, which Client will consider in good faith. If the performance problem is not corrected within thirty (30) days under that plan, Provider will replace the individual, and Client will bear the ordinary training cost for the replacement unless the removal was for cause.

(d) Hiring by Client. During the Term and for twelve (12) months afterwards, Client will not solicit for employment or hire any member of the Delivery Team or Key Staff without Provider’s written consent, which Provider may condition on payment of a conversion fee equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the individual’s annualised billing under the Agreement during the preceding twelve (12) months.
